record.paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Among complete noncompact finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space, are the only possible examples the standard hyperspheres, minimal hypersurfaces, and hypersurfaces of null 2-type?

evidence.quote: the following two conjectures on finite type hypersurfaces
Conjecture 7.3. The only complete non-compact hypersurfaces in a Euclidean space are standard hyperspheres, minimal hypersurfaces and hypersurfaces of null 2-type.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $x : M^n \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean $(n+1)$-space, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M^n$ acting componentwise on the position vector $x$. The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type if its position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $x_0 \in \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is constant and each non-constant $x_i$ ($i=1,\ldots,k$) satisfies $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for some real number $\lambda_i$, with the $\lambda_i$ pairwise distinct. The smallest such integer $k$ is called the type of $x$, and $M^n$ is then called a $k$-type submanifold. A finite-type submanifold is said to be of null $k$-type if one of the eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ in the above decomposition equals $0$. A minimal hypersurface is one whose mean curvature vector vanishes identically (equivalently $\Delta x = 0$). A standard hypersphere is a round sphere $S^n(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every complete noncompact finite-type hypersurface in Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is either a minimal hypersurface or a hypersurface of null $2$-type. (Equivalently, the only complete hypersurfaces of finite type in $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ are the standard hyperspheres, the minimal hypersurfaces, and the hypersurfaces of null $2$-type.)
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known conjecture of B.-Y. Chen on finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space. Recent surveys and research papers (e.g., on δ(2)- and δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces, and on related biharmonic problems) treat it as still-open, with progress only in special subcases such as small codimension restrictions, low number of distinct principal curvatures, or specific δ-ideal classes. No general resolution appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems and conjectures on submanifolds of finite type: recent development
status_evidence.snippet: Survey collecting open problems and conjectures on finite-type submanifolds, including the conjecture on complete noncompact finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is presented as an open problem in a recent survey of conjectures on finite-type submanifolds.

status_evidence.title: δ(2)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces of Euclidean space are spherical cylinders
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies δ(2)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space as open parts of spherical cylinders.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications of null 2-type hypersurfaces have been obtained, indicating the broader conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces, proving constant mean and scalar curvature in this subclass.
status_evidence.claim: Work continues to chip away at null 2-type hypersurface classification, consistent with the conjecture being unresolved.
